t: Minimum Right Shifts to Sort the Array — Rotation Detection
o: Right shifts rotate the array; the array is sortable iff it is a rotation of its sorted version. That happens iff there is EXACTLY ONE descent (index i with nums[i] > nums[i+1]); the answer is n − (i+1). Already-sorted arrays have zero descents → 0. [2,1,4] has a descent at 0 but the wrap-around piece 4 > 2 creates a second violation → −1.
k: Exactly one descent (plus wrap-around consistency) characterizes sortable rotations.

a.i: Locate the unique descent; verify both segments are internally sorted and the last element ≤ the first; answer = number of shifts bringing the minimum to front.
s: Count descents; if 0 return 0; if >1 return −1.
Check nums[k..n−1] sorted, nums[0..k−1] sorted, and nums[n−1] ≤ nums[0].
a.t: O(n) — one pass to find descents plus O(1) wrap-around check

w: The wrap-around comparison nums[n−1] ≤ nums[0] is the check people forget. Note the internal segments are automatically sorted when there's exactly one descent. Follow-up: minimum LEFT shifts (answer becomes k), or allow arbitrary rotations of subarrays.
